_readme: Every model input. type: measured = read from a primary source; derived = arithmetic on measured values; assumed = analyst judgement, shown with the range used. Edit and re-run scripts/06_model.py.

usd_per_engaged_hour_platform.source: Roblox Q2 2026 8-K: developer exchange fees $363M / 29B hours engaged = $0.0125 per engaged hour (Q2 2025: $316M / 27.4B = $0.0115). Hour-weighted platform mean, so dominated by top experiences.

small_game_monetisation_mult.source: Lognormal multiplier on the platform mean for a new solo game (90% interval ~0.13x-1.27x). Rationale: payouts are concentrated (top-1000 creators averaged $1.3M in 2025 vs ~$1.5B total DevEx => ~85% of payouts); third-party ARPDAU ranges for small games ($0.003-$0.025 per DAU-day, RoWatcher) sit at 0.1x-0.8x of the platform mean ($363M / (123M DAU x 91 d) = $0.032).

genre_index_absent.source: Monetisation index used when a Roblox genre has no entry among the 472 top-earning experiences.

genre_index_shrink_n.source: Pseudo-count shrinking the genre earnings-per-CCU index toward 1.0 when few top earners carry the genre.

genre_index_clip.source: Bounds on the genre index. Narrow on purpose: it is a rank-based proxy (revenue assumed ~1/earning-rank), so it is allowed to tilt results, not decide them.

genre_index_sigma.source: Log-sd of noise on the genre index (it is a rank-based proxy, not revenue).

prior_traction_odds.source: Prior odds that a competent, deliberately scoped solo release averages >=100 CCU for 12 months: median 3%, 90% interval ~0.8%-10%. Not measurable from public data. Bounded below by the unconditional rate (10,500 creators newly qualified for DevEx in 2025 out of 'millions of creators' => well under 1%) and above by the observation that only ~19,000 experiences have >=1 player at a time (RoWatcher, June 2026) and ~1,370 have >=1,000.

p_traction_cap.source: No amount of desk evidence justifies more than ~1-in-3.

traction_ccu.source: Definition of traction: 12-month average concurrent players. 100 CCU-years = 876,000 engaged hours.

pareto_alpha.source: Tail exponent of experiences by CCU. RoWatcher June 2026 counts: 1,370 experiences >=1,000 CCU; 112 >=10,000; 12 >=100,000 => per-decade survival 0.08-0.11 => alpha ~0.96-1.09. Own snapshot (Top Playing Now, ranks 10-98): CCU ~ rank^-0.89 => alpha ~1.12.

ccu_cap.source: Cap on a solo developer's 12-month average CCU (median CCU of top-earning ranks 1-50 is ~21,700, nearly all group-owned). Keeps the mean from being driven by lottery outcomes.

fail_ccu_median.source: Median 12-month average CCU of a release that does not get traction.

tail_value_mult.source: Revenue after month 12 as a multiple of first-year revenue, for games with traction. 227 of the 472 top earners are under 12 months old: lifecycles are short.

opportunity_wage_usd_h.source: Value of one developer hour. Set to your real alternative; sensitivity runs $0 and $40.

cash_test_usd.source: Triangular. Paid soft-launch test: Robux at ~$0.0125 each (400 R$ = $4.99) and 4-12 R$ per sponsored visit (third-party, DevForum-sourced range) => $250 buys roughly 1,700-5,000 visits. Plus icons/thumbnails.

overrun_median.source: Median schedule overrun multiplier on the three-point hour estimates (planning fallacy).

upkeep_months_if_fail.source: Months of upkeep spent before abandoning a launched game that gets no traction.

max_mvp_hours_solo.source: Stage-2 budget screen: likely MVP hours above this are out of scope for a first, cash-constrained solo project (4 full-time weeks).

brand_dependence_cut.source: If one franchise carries >=60% of an archetype's web attention, the demand is for the brand at least as much as for the mechanic.

lambda_risk.source: Risk aversion: V = E[profit] - lambda x E[loss]. lambda=1 means a lost dollar hurts twice as much as a gained dollar helps.

gates.source: Staged policy. Gate A (after 35% of MVP hours): hands-on fun test, weak filter. Gate B (after MVP + paid soft launch): retention/session metrics vs thresholds, assumed 85% sensitivity and 80% specificity for eventual traction. These error rates are not measured.

likelihood_ratios._note: type: assumed. Odds multipliers applied to the prior. WHICH bucket an archetype lands in is decided by measured data (see scripts/06_model.py buckets()); the multiplier RANGES are judgement, drawn log-uniformly each world. Ranges are deliberately narrow for web evidence (cross-archetype rank correlation between web share and Roblox CCU is reported in out/model_summary.json) and wider for evidence observed on Roblox itself.

genre_l2_min_n.source: Minimum number of top-472 earners in a sub-genre before its own index is used; otherwise the parent genre's index applies.

programme_hour_budgets.source: Total developer-hour budgets for the programme view (several staged bets in sequence).

age_gate_16plus_value_share.source: Share of platform spending power a new game can reach while it is still in the 16+ trial phase (before 250 highly engaged plays unlock Roblox Kids and Select). Derived in scripts/09_age_analysis.py from the Q2 2026 shareholder letter: 57% of DAUs age-checked; age-checked mix 35% under 13 / 38% 13-17 / 27% 18+; under-18 penetration 60%; U.S. 18+ monetise 'over 50% higher' than under-18. Assumes 40% of the 13-17 band is 16-17. Used only in a sensitivity scenario.

us18_devex_premium.source: Roblox, 30 Apr 2026: DevEx rate for eligible in-game spend by age-checked 18+ users in the U.S. is 42% higher ($0.0054 vs $0.0038 per Robux), effective 8 Jun 2026, R15 experiences only.

us18_spend_share_scenario.source: Scenario: share of a game's earned Robux that comes from eligible U.S. 18+ spend. Unknown for any given game.
